newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy rate cut expected, perhaps by Monday.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy rate cut expected, perhaps by Monday.

text.p: An impasse in talks on Italian metalworkers' contracts has cooled market expectations for a near term interest rate cut, but many analysts still expect the Bank of Italy to cut by at least 50 basis points by Monday.
Four Italian cities published preliminary December inflation data on Thursday, leading analysts to forecast December inflation at 2.6 percent year on year, the same as November.
Six more cities, Milan, Turin, Bologna, Genoa, Naples and Florence are due to announce their December consumer price data at 1630 GMT on Friday.
Analysts polled by Reuters said it would be a positive signal for markets if the data confirmed the 2.6 percent rate.
"This could be enough (for an interest rate cut)," Marco Ratti, analyst at Banca Commerciale Italiana, said.
The Bank of Italy last cut official rates on October 23, bringing the discount rate to 7.50 percent from 8.25 percent.
But on Thursday, shortly after the four sample cities released their figures, metalworkers' unions announced pay talks with employers' association Federmeccanica had collapsed.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has called the situation "very delicate" and economists said the impasse on the negotiations acted like a cold shower on interest rate expectations.
"It adds an element of uncertainty also because until yesterday morning, negotiations seemed to have reached a breakthrough," Fabio Stolfa, analyst at Caboto, said.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu had said on Thursday he hoped for a solution to the dispute by Saturday but Federmeccanica later said it considered this possibility "very remote".
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio recently sounded a note of caution on wage hikes, saying: "It is necessary that incomes evolve along a path that does not exceed productivity growth."
Analysts said economically a further delay in cutting rates would not be justified but the labour knot could reduce the size of an easing to 50 basis points instead of 75 basis points.

"The major knots on the 1997 budget law have already been untangled. The only obstacle is the metalworkers' contract renewal but it's hard to tell when it will be resolved. If they don't cut rates now, they will have missed a good opportunity," Renzo Avesani, economist at Italian savings bank Cariplo said.
"A delay in easing could disturb financial markets. But with the labour issue, a 50 basis point cut seems more probable than 75," Stolfa said.
Two analysts expected the Bank of Italy to wait for a positive conclusion to the labour negotiations.
Following are the results of the survey:
1. Will the Bank of Italy cut the official discount rate?
2. When?
By Monday 6/11
By the end of the year 3/11
After the renewal of the metalworkers' contract 2/11
3. By how much will the central bank cut rates?
Note - Banco di Roma, Banco di Sardegna, Caboto, Cariplo, BCI, Credit, Euromobiliare, Lehman Brothers, Nomura, Paribas, San Paolo Bank took part in the poll.
